Subject: Onboarding: TLS termination & internal DNS for private endpoints

Hi Sean / Laura,

Thanks again for the quick responses during the POC. Were starting to draft the production onboarding work for Nebulas private deployment (VPC peering + AWS Direct Connect) and we need a clear, actionable plan for TLS and DNS. A few constraints from our side:

- All control-plane traffic must be protected with mutual TLS.
- Customer-managed CA is preferred for audit reasons but we can consider Redwood-managed certs if we get cryptographic evidence and HSM integration.
- DNS must remain internal; we use Route53 private hosted zones per account.

Can you confirm the preferred termination patterns Redwood supports for private endpoints? Specifically:
1) Terminate TLS at our edge (ALB) and present mTLS to Redwood behind the private link, or
2) Let Redwood terminate TLS in your private runtime and present a short-lived client cert back to us?

Also please include recommended CN/SAN formats for certs, OCSP stapling expectations, cert rotation frequency, and any required DNS records (CNAME/A, delegated zones, SRV, etc.).

If you have a one-page runbook or checklist you can share thatd be ideal to share with our platform team. Ive attached our internal network map for context.

Thanks,
Sara

Subject: Re: Onboarding: TLS termination & internal DNS for private endpoints

Sara / team,

Below is an engineering run-through with concrete choices and a short handover checklist. Im keeping this focused on items that materially affect routing, certs, and auditability.

Architecture options (tradeoffs):
A) Customer-edge termination (recommended when Nebula wants full key custody):
  - TLS terminated at Nebula ALB/NGINX. Redwood connects over a private link using mTLS (client certs issued by Nebula CA).
  - Pros: Nebula retains full key control; easiest for audit.
  - Cons: Nebula must automate rotation and OCSP provisioning; healthcheck TLS config must match Redwood runtime expectations.

B) Redwood-edge termination (recommended when centralized automation is preferred):
  - TLS terminates in Redwood private runtime; Nebula presents a short-lived client cert to authenticate inbound requests or we use private peering + source-based control.
  - Pros: Seamless Redwood rotation, easier automation (ACME/automation on our side).
  - Cons: Nebula needs to trust Redwood-managed cert chain (we can cross-sign with your PCA or provide HSM attestation).

DNS recommendations (private zones):
- Use a per-environment private hosted zone: e.g., nebula.internal.redwood.io (or delegated subdomain under your private zone).
- A records for load balancers, SRV only if your setup uses service discovery (not required for basic endpoints).
- TTL: 60-300s depending on how often you plan to rotate endpoints during failover.
- Configure healthcheck endpoints (TCP/TLS ALPN) with short intervals if you rely on LB-based failover.

Cert shape and SANs:
- SANs: include explicit hostnames (api.staging.nebula.redwoodprivate, controlplane.nebula.redwoodprivate) and wildcard only if you accept the broader blast radius.
- CN: legacy support only; use SANs for all modern clients.
- TLS versions: require TLS 1.3 for control-plane paths; enable TLS 1.2 only if an older client forces it.
- OCSP: prefer stapling from the termination point; if using customer PCA, ensure OCSP responder is reachable from the termination location.

Rotation & automation:
- Rotation frequency: 90 days recommended for leaf certs; use short-lived certs (7-30 days) for mTLS client certs if possible.
- Automation: ACME + internal ACME CA, or AWS ACM PCA + Lambda rotation hooks. We can integrate with your PCA via SCEP/ACME if you provide an ingress ACME endpoint.

mTLS specifics:
- Client certs: recommend mTLS both directions for control-plane (client & server verify).
- PKI model: if you run PCA, issue an intermediate for Redwood with constrained EKU for authentication.

Operational notes:
- SNI: Redwood runtime will honor SNI; ensure LB preserves the client SNI header.
- ALPN: use h2 or http/1.1 depending on runtime; prefer h2 for multiplexing.
- Logging: include TLS handshake logs and cert serials in audit logs; we recommend 90-day retention for cert audit entries.

Action items (short list):
- [Hiro] Draft cert CN/SAN template + sample CSR by 2026-11-18.
- [Priyom] Provide HSM/KMS acceptance criteria and required evidence (HSM attestation, key policy) by 2026-11-19.
- [Laura] Confirm DNS delegation approach (private hosted zone vs delegation) and provide zone IDs by 2026-11-18.
- [Sara/Pete] Confirm whether Nebula will run PCA or prefer Redwood-managed certs by 2026-11-17.

Ive attached the internal checklist (nebula_private_ca_checklist.xlsx) and put the runbook outline into the shared drive link in my earlier mail. Ill walk through this with the team in the scheduled call.

-Hiro

Subject: Re: Onboarding: TLS termination & internal DNS for private endpoints

Couple of compliance/security items to call out before we pick a termination model:

- Key custody & evidence: If Nebula insists on customer-managed keys, we need: HSM attestation, key rotation policy, and proof of access controls (IAM roles + MFA for key usage). If Redwood manages keys, we must provide exportable audit logs and KMS/HSM attestation for SOC2.
- Mutual TLS: require client cert revocation plan. Short-lived client certs reduce CRL size but you must provide automation to replace them.
- PKI hierarchy: prefer issuing an intermediate from Nebulas PCA dedicated to Redwood with an EKU-limited profile for authentication. That makes audit scoping easier.
- Evidence package: list of artifacts we need for compliance (HSM certs, key rotation logs, KMS access logs, CA policy doc). Ill prepare a template.
- Network proof: for split-DNS or private delegation we need a traceroute + firewall policy snapshot to validate that no public route exists to the endpoints.

Pilot recommendation: run the staging pilot with Nebula-managed PCA and customer-edge termination first. This provides the cleanest audit trail and lets us validate rotation automation before we consider Redwood-managed certs for production.

Ill upload the compliance checklist to the shared drive and tag the JIRA INFRA-2983 with the required evidence items.

- Priyom
